title: Enterprise Onboarding: Comprehensive Playbook, Escalation, Integration, Known Issues, Health Checks & QBRs
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This document is the canonical Enterprise Onboarding & Support Playbook for Redwood Inference customers. It consolidates the standard onboarding phases, integration checklist, escalation playbook, a curated list of known issues and workarounds, the support / ticketing process, and recurring health-check and QBR materials. It is intended for Customer Success Managers (CSMs), Solutions Engineers (SEs), Support Engineers, and on-call SREs supporting enterprise customers.

Goals:
- Provide a repeatable, low-friction onboarding path that reduces time-to-first-successful-inference to < 2 weeks for typical integrations.
- Define clear escalation paths and SLAs so customers know who to contact and when.
- Ensure operational readiness: monitoring, alerts, runbooks, and canary policies are in place for production launches.
- Provide QBR-ready artifacts and cadence to align with customer success outcomes.

Ownership and Roles:
- Customer Success (owner): Aisha Patel (Primary), Diego Martinez (Secondary)
- Solutions Engineering: Renee Chen (Integration Lead)
- Support / Escalations: Markus Feldmann (Support Lead)
- Eng-SRE: Pager rotation and on-call documented in /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks
- Product: Product PM for the customer (assigned per contract)

Onboarding Phases (high level):
1) Discovery (Week 0-1)
   - Kickoff call: Introductions, objectives, success metrics, security checklist, and timeline. Use onboarding kickoff template: templates/onboarding-kickoff-brief.md
   - Deliverables: Project plan, contact matrix, network allowlist (IP ranges), data classification.
2) Integration & Development (Week 1-3)
   - Integration options: Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private (VPC). Confirm chosen deployment mode and network topology.
   - Provide API/SDK quickstart, example repo, and Postman collection. Example call (curl):
     curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate 
       -H "Authorization: Bearer ${API_KEY}" 
       -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
       -d '{"model":"redwood-v1", "input":"Translate to French: Hello"}'
   - Integration checklist (must pass before validation):
     - Authentication: API keys or OIDC configured and validated.
     - Network: TLS, allowlist, and if Private deployment, VPN/VPC peering tests passed.
     - Schema: Logging and observability hooks integrated (request IDs, customer_id)
     - Rate limits: Non-production rate-limited to 10 RPS until validated.
3) Validation & Load Testing (Week 2-4)
   - Run synthetic workload (provided in eval-harness repo) to validate latency and throughput. Baseline SLO targets: P50 <= 120ms, P95 <= 450ms for typical generation workloads on Hosted; Dedicated targets specified in contract.
   - Run safety/quality checks using customer prompt-sets and Redwood Optimize recommendations.
   - Failure modes and rollback plan defined.
4) Go-Live and Stabilization (Week 3-6)
   - Production burn-in for 48-72 hours with live traffic ramp. Monitor key metrics: token volume, cost per 1k tokens, latency P50/P95, error rate, and cache hit rate.
   - Canaries and rollout policy: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 24-72 hours with manual gates.
5) Ongoing Success (Post Go-Live)
   - Quarterly QBR cadence, monthly health checks for first 3 months, then monthly/quarterly per contract.

Integration Guide (detailed):
- Deployment mode decisions: summary table
  - Hosted: fastest onboarding, pay-as-you-go, Redwood manages infra.
  - Dedicated: reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, requires network config and scheduled maintenance windows.
  - Private: customer-managed control plane, requires onprem packaging, KMS/HSM integration.
- Example environment variables for SDK:
  - REDWOOD_API_KEY=prod_xxx
  - REDWOOD_REGION=us-west-2
  - REDWOOD_RUNTIME=dedicated
- Logging and observability: include request_id and model_version in every request. Example JSON logging snippet: {"request_id": "${REQ_ID}", "model": "redwood-v1", "latency_ms": ${LATENCY}}
- Caching & batching: Recommended defaults for high-throughput inference: batch_size=32, max_wait_ms=12. For latency-sensitive workloads, batch_size <= 8 and max_wait_ms=6.
- Security checklist (minimum):
  - Enforce TLS 1.2+, mTLS for Private deployments if required.
  - KMS integration for key management (customer-managed keys supported for Private).
  - Audit logging enabled and forwarded to customer SIEM per contract.

Escalation Playbook:
- Severity definitions and target response times:
  - Sev 1 (Critical): Total service outage or > 50% request failure for > 15 minutes for production traffic. Response: 15 minutes. Owners: Support Lead -> Eng-SRE on-call -> Engineering Pager.
  - Sev 2 (High): Significant degradation (P95 latency > 3x baseline or error rate > 5% for 30 minutes). Response: 60 minutes. Owners: Support Engineer -> SE -> Eng-SRE.
  - Sev 3 (Medium): Functional impact to a subset of users or non-blocking feature regressions. Response: 4 business hours.
  - Sev 4 (Low): Cosmetic or feature requests, non-urgent. Response: 3 business days.
- Escalation matrix (contact order):
  1) Customer Success / CSM (Primary)
  2) Support (support@redwood.example) -> creates ticket in Zendesk/JIRA with tags: customer:<customer-id>, severity:<sev>
  3) Solutions Engineering (for integration/config issues)
  4) Eng-SRE / On-call (for infrastructure/runtime issues)
  5) Product / Core engineering (for model or runtime bugs)
- Communication templates: Use the incident communication template in templates/incident-comm.md for customer updates (first update within 30 minutes for Sev1).
- Runbook links (operational):
  - On-call playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/oncall-playbook
  - Model fallback runbook: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/fallback-to-variant

Support Process and Ticketing:
- Ticket intake: All customer issues must be logged in Zendesk. For enterprise customers, tickets are mirrored into JIRA (project RED-CS).
- Triage SLA: Support triages within 1 hour for Sev1/Sev2, 6 hours for Sev3.
- Ownership: Support assigns the ticket and tags owner_team and product_area. Tickets must contain: reproduction steps, logs (redwood_request_id), timestamp, and customer environment details.
- Escalation criteria examples:
  - Reproducible data corruption or model hallucination rate above agreed threshold -> escalate to Product and Applied ML.
  - Latency regressions after a deployment affecting >10% of requests -> escalate to Eng-SRE.
- Post-incident procedure: Fill out postmortem template within 72 hours for Sev1 and Sev2 incidents affecting production SLAs. Link: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/postmortem-template.md

Known Issues & Workarounds (curated):
- Issue: Cold KV-cache spikes causing transient P95 latency increases.
  - Symptom: P95 jumps for first ~30k tokens after model is warmed.
  - Workaround: Enable prefix caching for common prompts and perform warmup runs using the eval-harness warmup.sh script. Recommended warmup pattern: 5-10 representative requests at max sequence length before go-live.
- Issue: Tokenization mismatch for non-UTF8 inputs (rare).
  - Symptom: "Invalid token" errors or truncated output.
  - Workaround: Normalize client inputs to NFC Unicode and enforce UTF-8 at ingress. See SDK helper: utils/utf8-normalize.py.
- Issue: Rate-limit H12 errors during bulk ingestion.
  - Symptom: 429s with header X-RateLimit-Reset > 30s.
  - Workaround: Implement exponential backoff with jitter. Recommended backoff: base=200ms, factor=2, max=60s. For large imports, request a temporary rate limit increase via support ticket.
- Issue: Occasional model divergence after quantization profile changes on Dedicated instances.
  - Symptom: Small but measurable drop in quality on targeted prompts.
  - Workaround: Pin model version to last-good variant and open ticket to schedule a canary rollout for the quantized variant. Use Redwood Optimize to generate evaluation diff report.

Health Checks & QBR Materials:
- Monthly health check checklist (for the first 3 months):
  - Usage summary: tokens/day, embeddings calls, peak qps.
  - Performance: P50, P95 latency, 99th percentile error rate. Thresholds: error_rate < 1% default; if >1%, root cause and mitigate.
  - Cost review: Cost per 1k tokens and recommendations for batching/quantization.
  - Observability: Ensure traced requests are >= 5% of traffic and sampled across routes.
  - Security: Confirm audit logs forwarded and retention policy matches contract.
- QBR template sections (quarterly):
  1) Executive summary with key metrics and outcomes.
  2) Usage trends and forecasting.
  3) Reliability review (incidents, MTTR, open action items).
  4) Model quality and regression alerts (prompt-set evals).
  5) Cost optimization opportunities (autoscaling, quantization, batching).
  6) Roadmap asks and feature requests.
- Deliverables: QBR slide deck (template in templates/qbr-template.pptx), health-check JSON export (automated from Redwood Console reports), and action item tracker (JIRA board: RED-CS-QBR).

Templates and Checklists (quick access):
- Onboarding project plan (templates/onboarding-project-plan.md)
- Security / network checklist (templates/network-security-checklist.md)
- Canaries and rollout verification checklist (templates/canary-verification.md)
- Incident communication and customer update templates (templates/incident-comm.md)

Appendices:
A) Example escalation email for Sev1:
Subject: [SEV1][Customer: AcmeCorp] Production outage impacting inference
Body:
We are actively investigating a Sev1 outage impacting inference for AcmeCorp. Current observations: 60% request failures, affected routes: /v1/generate, first seen at 2026-03-03T18:02:00Z. Next update in 30 minutes.
B) Quick SLO reference:
- Availability SLO (hosted): 99.95% monthly uptime
- Latency SLO (hosted): P95 < 450ms for standard generation model workloads
- Support response SLA: 15 minutes for Sev1, 60 minutes for Sev2

C) Useful internal links:
- Eng-SRE runbooks: /confluence/eng-sre/runbooks
- Model onboarding: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/model-onboarding
- Observability standards: /confluence/architecture-and-standards/observability-standards

If you are updating this playbook, please follow the Confluence doc standards: keep content structured, date major changes in the changelog at the top of the body, and request review from Support Lead and Eng-SRE for operational changes.
